title: List Proposals Request
description: Read the seller's current proposals for an account, optionally narrowed to opportunities or proposal IDs. Experimental (media_buy.open_opportunities): sellers implementing it MUST list the feature id in experimental_features. Each invocation completes synchronously and never mutates proposal or opportunity state. It is the authoritative current-state and repair read for proposal.created notifications, for proposal.offered notifications (the buy-scoped sibling for seller offers against accepted media buys, defined with media_buy.seller_offers), and for proposal records in list_account_changes; buyers use the notification or the change feed to learn that something changed, not routine polling. Results are visible to every principal the seller authorizes for the account, the same as other account-scoped reads, and never cross accounts.
x-tool-summary: List the seller's current proposals and their lifecycle state for an account or opportunity.

adcp_version.description: Release-precision AdCP version (VERSION.RELEASE, e.g. "3.0", "3.1", "3.1-beta"). On a request: the buyer's release pin — the seller validates against its supported_versions and returns VERSION_UNSUPPORTED on cross-major mismatch, or downshifts to the highest supported release within the same major. On a response: the release the seller actually served — clients SHOULD validate the response against that release's schema, not against their pin. Patches are not negotiated; surface them as build_version on capabilities for operational visibility. When omitted, falls back to adcp_major_version (deprecated) or server default. Buyers SHOULD emit both adcp_version and adcp_major_version through 3.x to remain compatible with sellers that only read the legacy field. NORMALIZATION: SDKs that read full-semver values from bundle metadata (e.g. ComplianceIndex.published_version = "3.1.0-beta.1") MUST normalize to release-precision ("3.1-beta.1") before emitting on the wire — meta-field values are NOT valid wire values.

adcp_major_version.description: DEPRECATED in favor of adcp_version (release-precision string). Servers MUST continue to honor this field through 3.x. Removed in 4.0. Original semantics: the AdCP major version the buyer's payloads conform to. Sellers validate against their supported major_versions and return VERSION_UNSUPPORTED if unsupported. When omitted, the seller assumes its highest supported version.

idempotency_key.description: Optional replay key accepted uniformly on read calls.

context_id.description: MCP compatibility field: servers ignore this value; A2A uses transport-native Message/Task contextId.

allOf.title: Context Object
allOf.description: Opaque correlation data that is echoed unchanged in responses. Used for internal tracking, UI session IDs, trace IDs, and other caller-specific identifiers that don't affect protocol behavior. Context data is never parsed by AdCP agents - it's simply preserved and returned.

allOf.title: Push Notification Config
allOf.description: Webhook configuration for asynchronous task notifications. Uses A2A-compatible PushNotificationConfig structure. By default, webhooks are signed with the AdCP RFC 9421 profile (see docs/building/by-layer/L1/security.mdx#webhook-callbacks) — the seller signs outbound with a key published at the jwks_uri on its own brand.json `agents[]` entry and the buyer verifies against that JWKS, so no shared secret crosses the wire. The optional `authentication` block carries credentials for the legacy Bearer or HMAC-SHA256 fallback (deprecated; removed in AdCP 4.0). Note: the `idempotency_key` that receivers dedup on lives inside the webhook **payload** body (see docs/building/by-layer/L3/webhooks.mdx#reliability and the mcp-webhook-payload schema), not in this configuration object — this schema only describes the receiver-side transport config sent to the seller. This schema is designed for composition via allOf - consuming schemas should define their own additionalProperties constraints.

url.description: Webhook endpoint URL for task status notifications. The wire contract is unconstrained beyond `format: "uri"` — in particular, publishers SHOULD NOT enforce a destination-port allowlist by default, since buyers legitimately host receivers on non-standard TLS ports (`:9443`, `:4443`, path-routed multi-tenant gateways). The SSRF guard the protocol relies on is the IP-range check + DNS-rebinding-resistant connect pin defined in [Webhook URL validation (SSRF)](/docs/building/by-layer/L1/security#webhook-url-validation-ssrf), not port filtering. Operators who want a hardened destination-port allowlist as defense-in-depth (e.g., locked-down enterprise egress) opt in explicitly — see [Destination port: permissive by default](/docs/building/by-layer/L1/security#destination-port-permissive-by-default).

operation_id.description: Buyer-supplied correlation identifier for the operation that will produce webhooks against this registration. The seller MUST echo this value verbatim into every webhook payload's `operation_id` field (see [`mcp-webhook-payload.json`](/schemas/core/mcp-webhook-payload.json) and [Webhooks — Operation IDs](/docs/building/by-layer/L3/webhooks#operation-ids-and-url-templates)). Buyers SHOULD generate a unique value per task invocation (UUID recommended). This field is the canonical registration channel for `operation_id`; buyers MAY additionally embed routing values in the URL path or query as an aid for their own HTTP server, but the URL is opaque to the seller and the wire-level source of truth is this field. Sellers MUST NOT parse the URL to recover `operation_id`. For 3.x schema compatibility the member remains optional, but a seller MUST reject a task that registers an AdCP webhook without it using `INVALID_REQUEST`; otherwise the required webhook envelope cannot be emitted.

token.description: Optional client-provided token for webhook validation. The seller MUST echo this value verbatim in every webhook payload's `token` field (see [`mcp-webhook-payload.json`](/schemas/core/mcp-webhook-payload.json) for the receiver-side validation obligation). Length bounds give receivers a defensive range check on the echoed value; senders SHOULD generate tokens with at least 128 bits of entropy (≥22 base64url characters). This is a complementary authenticity mechanism that can layer on top of the RFC 9421 webhook signature — unlike the `authentication` block below, it is not on the 4.0 removal track. Receivers that registered both a signing key (RFC 9421) and a `token` MUST NOT treat a valid token echo as authorization to skip signature verification; both checks remain independent obligations.

authentication.description: Legacy authentication configuration (A2A-compatible), deprecated; removed in AdCP 4.0. Sending this block asks the seller for Bearer or HMAC-SHA256 instead of RFC 9421 signing; omitting it selects the profile that `signing_profile` names. A seller whose `webhook_signing.legacy_hmac_fallback` is `false` rejects the registration with `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE` and `error.field` pointing at it. A seller MUST NOT sign the same webhook both ways, and a buyer MUST NOT try 9421 first and fall back to HMAC. The seller's 9421 webhook key is published at its brand.json `agents[]` `jwks_uri` with `adcp_use: "request-signing"` (deprecated `webhook-signing` keys stay accepted during the compatibility window). See docs/building/by-layer/L1/security.mdx#webhook-callbacks, including the `webhook_mode_mismatch` rejection buyers apply on a mode mismatch.

schemes.description: Array of authentication schemes. Supported: ['Bearer'] for simple token auth, ['HMAC-SHA256'] for legacy shared-secret signing. Both are deprecated; new integrations SHOULD omit `authentication` and use the RFC 9421 webhook profile.

items.title: Authentication Scheme
items.description: Legacy authentication schemes for the webhook auth block. Bearer: token sent in Authorization header. HMAC-SHA256: legacy shared-secret signing. Both are deprecated; new integrations SHOULD omit the authentication block and use the RFC 9421 webhook signing profile (applicable on schemas where authentication is optional). Removed in AdCP 4.0.

credentials.description: Credentials for the legacy scheme. For Bearer: token sent in Authorization header. For HMAC-SHA256: shared secret used to generate signature. Minimum 32 characters. Exchanged out-of-band during onboarding.

signing_profile.title: Webhook Signing Profile
signing_profile.description: Webhook-signing profile the seller uses for every delivery to this `url`. When it is omitted, the seller signs with `adcp/webhook-signing/v1`, or with the legacy scheme when `authentication` is present. A seller whose `webhook_signing.profiles` does not list it rejects the registration with `INVALID_REQUEST`. MUST NOT be combined with `authentication`.

push_notification_config.description: Uniform per-call envelope field accepted for SDK compatibility. This does not register a subscription; proposal.created subscribers are registered through sync_accounts notification_configs.

allOf.title: Canonical Account Reference
allOf.description: Compact advertiser-account reference for canonical 3.2 tools. Uses either the seller/storefront account_id, which is the account's identity, or the buyer-declared natural key without BrandRef inline overrides. The natural key is brand + operator; its optional brand.countries, operator_unit.id, currency, timezone, and sandbox fields are account attributes that act as lookup filters, matched as in account-ref.json. A natural key resolves only when exactly one of the caller's accounts matches; otherwise the seller returns ACCOUNT_AMBIGUOUS. brand.countries does not target delivery; operator_unit.name is display metadata and never filters.

brand.title: Brand Key
brand.description: Stable brand identity used to resolve the canonical brand manifest. A brand is its domain plus brand_id where that domain's brand.json lists several brands. The manifest URL is derived from domain; callers do not send brand assets or per-call brand overrides. countries is an account attribute, not part of the brand's identity, and does not target delivery.

domain.description: Domain that hosts /.well-known/brand.json or is registered for the brand.

brand_id.title: Brand ID
brand_id.description: Brand within a brand.json that lists several brands. Omit for a single-brand domain.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries the advertiser account serves. This is an account attribute: it does not identify the brand or the account, and it is not delivery targeting. Omit when the account is not limited to particular countries. Array order is not meaningful.

operator_unit.title: Operator Unit
operator_unit.description: Optional operator-owned business unit, agency seat, or platform account. An account attribute: id acts as a lookup filter; name is display metadata and never filters.

id.description: Stable identifier assigned by the operator. Numeric platform IDs and durable slugs are both valid. Scoped by the enclosing operator domain.

name.description: Human-readable seat or business-unit name, such as Nova EMEA. This display label may change and never filters a natural-key lookup.

currency.description: ISO 4217 transaction currency when the advertiser object is currency-bound. An account attribute that acts as a lookup filter; all media buys on the account use it. Omit for per-media-buy currency selection.

timezone.description: Account timezone. An account attribute that acts as a lookup filter, sent only for buyer-selected account_fixed accounts.

opportunity_ids.description: Return only proposals associated with these opportunities. Proposals created without an opportunity are returned only when no opportunity_ids filter is supplied.

media_buy_ids.description: Return only proposals whose snapshot media_buy_id is one of these buys: seller offers and other amendments against those buys, plus the accepted snapshots that created them. Proposals with no media_buy_id are returned only when no media_buy_ids filter is supplied. Unknown or inaccessible IDs are omitted, not errors. Combines with the other filters as an AND.

proposal_ids.description: Return only these proposals. Unknown or inaccessible IDs are omitted, not errors.

dispositions.description: Return only proposals in these dispositions. Defaults to every disposition. Terminal snapshots are retained for at least 30 days after their disposition changed.

items.title: Proposal Disposition
items.description: Seller-tracked lifecycle disposition of one immutable proposal snapshot, returned by list_proposals next to the unchanged snapshot. Distinct from proposal_status (draft, committed, accepted), which is part of the snapshot and never changes after issue. Sellers MUST keep a snapshot readable through list_proposals while it is available and for at least 30 days after it becomes accepted, declined, expired, or withdrawn; after that, get_media_buys remains the record for accepted terms. Experimental (media_buy.open_opportunities).

enumDescriptions.available: The snapshot can still be acted on: refined, declined, or, when committed and before expires_at, accepted. An outstanding seller offer whose base_media_buy_revision no longer matches the media buy is never available; see withdrawn. Buyers MUST NOT cache this value, because it can change without a notification. A refined source stays available unless the seller withdraws it; refinement creates new snapshots and does not retire the source.
enumDescriptions.accepted: The snapshot was executed through accept_proposal or create_media_buy. proposal_status on the snapshot is unchanged; the acceptance record is on the resulting media buy.
enumDescriptions.declined: The buyer declined the snapshot through decline_proposals. Terminal.
enumDescriptions.expired: expires_at passed before acceptance. For a committed snapshot the inventory hold is released. Terminal.
enumDescriptions.withdrawn: The seller retracted a draft snapshot before expiry, for example because the inventory sold. Terminal. A seller MUST NOT withdraw a committed snapshot before its expires_at, with one exception: an outstanding seller offer (origin seller_offer, not yet accepted, declined, or expired) made stale by a revision of the media buy, meaning its base_media_buy_revision no longer matches the buy's current revision. The seller MUST derive that state from the buy's current revision at read time and report such an offer withdrawn, never available, with disposition_changed_at set to the revision time. A revision made by accepting the offer itself is not a staleness event, and terminal dispositions never change. The offer stays readable under the retention rule and cannot be accepted. Sellers reject refine_proposals and accept_proposal for a withdrawn snapshot with INVALID_STATE, as for a declined one. There is no withdrawal notification: buyers see it through list_proposals or, when the seller implements the account change feed, a status_changed proposal record.

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

allOf.title: AdCP Version Envelope
allOf.description: Release-precision AdCP protocol version negotiation fields, defined once. Request schemas compose this envelope directly through `allOf`. Strict (`additionalProperties: false`) request schemas also redeclare these two fields in their own `properties` via `$ref`, because draft-07 does not evaluate properties across `allOf`. The Trusted Match match requests are the exception: they inline both fields for their strict privacy boundary. On a request, these fields are part of the request payload: the buyer's version pin. Responses do not compose this envelope directly. `core/protocol-envelope.json` composes it, so on a response `adcp_version` and `adcp_major_version` are envelope fields that the server framework stamps beside `status`, `task_id` and the other protocol-layer fields, not task body data.

Catch-up scan for the live offers against one accepted media buy, for example after missed proposal.offered notifications
